title: The inner retreat
hook: Marcus: people seek retreats by the sea, but you can retire into your own mind at any hour (Meditations 4.3)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the caged parrot played dead and flew free. Die before you die: let the performing self fall still.

Everybody has a dream escape. A cabin in the mountains. A week on a beach with no phone. A little house by a lake where nobody can reach you. You scroll through pictures of them at your desk and count the days until vacation. Then the vacation comes, and on the second day, lying by the water, you're still replaying the argument from work. An emperor who could have had any villa in the Roman world noticed this too, and wrote down where he thought the real retreat was. Today, the inner retreat.
screen: `A CABIN, A BEACH, A LAKE.` → `STILL REPLAYING THE ARGUMENT.` → `THE INNER RETREAT.`

segments.voice: Meditations 4.3 begins, in George Long's translation: "Men seek retreats for themselves, houses in the country, sea-shores, and mountains." Marcus admits he wants them too, very much. Then he pushes back on himself. You can, whenever you choose, retire into yourself. Nowhere is quieter, or freer from trouble, than your own mind, especially if you keep in it certain thoughts that bring calm the moment you look at them. Then the instruction, plainly: "Constantly then give to thyself this retreat, and renew thyself." Keep the principles short, he says, so they're ready. He names two. First, things out in the world don't reach inside you by themselves; your trouble comes from the opinion you form about them. Second, everything you see is changing and will soon be gone. That second one opens tomorrow. Notice what kind of retreat this is. Not an escape from your life, but a room inside it, one you can step into on a crowded train, in a hospital waiting room, in the middle of a hard meeting, and come out renewed. Yesterday Rumi's parrot found freedom by letting the performing self fall still. Today Marcus finds it by stepping inward for a moment. Different traditions, different words, and neither needs the other. But both say the cage and the country house aren't the final word. There's somewhere to go that no one can take from you. The inner retreat.
screen: `HOUSES, SEA-SHORES, MOUNTAINS.` · `RETIRE INTO YOURSELF, ANY HOUR.` · `KEEP THE PRINCIPLES SHORT.` · `A ROOM INSIDE YOUR LIFE.` · then, large: `THE INNER RETREAT.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes if that's comfortable, and picture a door into a quiet room inside you, where nobody else can come. Take one short, steadying thought in with you: this will pass, or I am here, or only this moment. Breathe slowly and rest there, then step back out, renewed, into wherever you are.
Renew thyself, Marcus's own instruction in Meditations 4.3: step back into your mind at any hour, and come out renewed. Today's word.
Your line: come out renewed. The quietest room is the one inside. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Many readers of the Meditations practice 4.3 as a short pause during the day, withdrawing into a few steadying thoughts, and modern Stoic practice often calls it the inner citadel.
